audit_scope.description: Auditing EL components (precompiles, EVM opcodes, block state transitions, transaction processing) and CL interfaces (beacon chain withdrawals, deposit requests, beacon roots).

execution_layer.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion attacks via gas-intensive precompile calls (ModExp, identity with large inputs), transient storage memory exhaustion.
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks with crafted state roots, malformed transaction payloads targeting precompile edge cases.

consensus_layer.threat: Propose blocks with invalid beacon roots, forge withdrawal requests, submit conflicting attestations.
Provide incorrect block data, censorship, denial of service on system contract calls.

misclassified_entities.reason: SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe) is an internal protocol constant used as the origin for system transactions, not an external entity. It is hardcoded and not controlled by any external actor.
Contract source code is a data artifact, not an external entity that actively sends data into the system at runtime. EIP-1803 is about opcode naming conventions with no runtime security implications.
Deployed contract bytecode is data already stored on-chain, not an external entity. The bytecode was validated at deployment time.
Wallet browser extensions (EIP-5749) operate in the browser environment, not at the EL/CL protocol level. Out of scope for this EL/CL audit.
DApp providing ABI specs (EIP-7896) is a wallet-level interaction, not an EL/CL protocol-level entity. Out of scope.
Same as EXT-DAPP - wallet-level interaction, out of scope for EL/CL protocol audit.
Trusted ABI database (EIP-7896) is a wallet-level resource, not an EL/CL protocol entity. Out of scope.
DApp user / wallet user in EIP-5749/EIP-7896 context is a browser-level interaction, out of scope. Users interact with EL via transactions (covered by EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-VIA-RPC).

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user or application can submit transactions via the public JSON-RPC API. No authentication required. Transaction data is fully untrusted and must be validated (nonce, balance, signature, gas, EIP-1559 fees, blob hashes). Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER from Prague fork and general user-submitted transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract/EOA via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input data. Input is fully untrusted. Covers EXT-CALLER, EXT-UNTRUSTED-CALLER, EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER, EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT across identity, ModExp, and ECRECOVER precompiles, plus EXT-CALLER (runtime message caller).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P / Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers (validators) propose blocks that must be fully validated: header checks, state root verification, transaction root, receipt root, gas used. A malicious validator could propose invalid blocks. All block data is untrusted and requires complete validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with EL via the Engine API, authenticated with JWT. The channel is authenticated but payload content (beacon roots, withdrawal data, deposit requests, consolidation requests) must still be validated. Covers EXT-BEACON-CHAIN providing withdrawal/deposit/consolidation data and beacon root for system transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any account can deploy arbitrary bytecode. The deployed bytecode is then subject to jump destination analysis and execution. Malicious bytecode could attempt to exploit JUMPDEST validation or opcode execution edge cases.

trusted_external_entities.name: DoS Attacker via Transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker submitting transactions designed to exhaust node resources via underpriced ModExp calls, large identity precompile inputs, transient storage memory exhaustion (~9.15MB per 30M gas tx), or large MCOPY operations. Covers EXT-ATTACKER from ModExp DoS model. Gas pricing mechanisms (minimum 200 gas floor, quadratic memory costs) are the primary defense.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: peer nodes on the P2P network can send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks. All data from peers is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P/Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: validators can propose invalid blocks with incorrect beacon roots, forge withdrawal requests, or submit conflicting attestations. The CL must validate all incoming data.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: ECDSA signature recovery, nonce check, balance sufficiency, gas limit vs block gas, EIP-1559 fee validation (max_priority_fee <= max_fee_per_gas, max_fee >= base_fee), blob versioned hash validation (KZG version 0x01), sender EOA or valid delegation check.

Gas metering must correctly bound resource usage. Input data of any size and content is accepted. Gas cost formula (GAS_IDENTITY + GAS_IDENTITY_WORD * ceil32(len)/32) must prevent resource exhaustion.

Gas formula (max(200, floor(complexity * iteration_count / 3))) must accurately reflect computational cost. Minimum 200 gas floor prevents spam. Input lengths (base_length, exponent_length, modulus_length) are parsed from untrusted calldata and drive gas computation.

Input validation: v must be 27 or 28, r and s must be in range (0, SECP256K1N). Invalid inputs return empty output (not revert). secp256k1_recover library must be correctly implemented. Note: high-S values (s > SECP256K1N/2) are NOT rejected at precompile level.

Complete block validation required: header validation (gas limits, base fee, timestamps, difficulty, nonce, parent hash), ommers hash == EMPTY_OMMER_HASH, state root verification, transaction root verification, receipt root verification, gas used verification. Invalid blocks must be rejected.

Beacon root data from CL is delivered via authenticated Engine API (JWT). System contracts at BEACON_ROOTS_ADDRESS and HISTORY_STORAGE_ADDRESS must exist with valid code. System transactions use SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS (30M) budget. Failures raise InvalidBlock.

Withdrawal data (validator addresses and amounts) comes from CL via Engine API. Amounts are converted Gwei to Wei (multiply by 10^9). Balance increases must be applied correctly. Withdrawal request predeploy contract must exist.

Deposit requests parsed from transaction logs. Withdrawal and consolidation requests obtained from predeploy contracts. Requests must maintain ascending type ordering. Request predeploy contracts must exist and return valid data.

Bytecode is immutable after deployment. Jump destination analysis must correctly distinguish JUMPDEST opcodes from PUSH data bytes. PUSH data containing 0x5B must not be treated as valid JUMPDEST. Analysis must handle arbitrary bytecode length within gas-bounded constraints.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Precompile gas metering, transient storage allocation, MCOPY memory operations
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Gas pricing must prevent resource exhaustion: ModExp minimum 200 gas floor, identity per-word gas, MCOPY quadratic memory cost, transient storage bounded by 100 gas per TSTORE (~9.15MB max per 30M gas tx). Implementations must not allocate excessive memory for intermediate buffers.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block and transaction propagation (devp2p eth protocol)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All blocks and transactions received from peers must be fully validated before processing. Eclipse attack mitigations must be in place. Invalid data must be rejected without excessive resource consumption.

All proposed blocks must be validated against consensus rules. Attestations must be checked for validity and slashing conditions. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing. Beacon roots provided to EL must be from validated beacon blocks.

coverage_analysis.notes: 8 out-of-scope entities (EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION, EXT-DAPP, EXT-MALICIOUS-DAPP, EXT-TRUSTED-DB, EXT-USER in browser context, EXT-CONTRACT-SOURCE, EXT-BYTECODE-SOURCE) were reclassified as misclassified. 1 entity (EXT-SYSTEM-ADDRESS) was identified as an internal protocol constant. All remaining in-scope entities have at least one boundary edge. Archetypal attack vectors (peer nodes, malicious validators) added as entities even where not explicitly present in subgraphs.
